column1: {{c1::Managed Identity}} avoids application-managed API keys for supported Azure AI calls.
column2:
Azure manages the identity's credentials, but the identity still needs service permissions.
Review source

column1: SQL's external REST procedure requires {{c1::HTTPS}} with TLS encryption.
column2:
Transport encryption does not replace authentication or authorization.
Review source

column1: For a logical-server object returned by Get-AzSqlServer, Identity.{{c1::PrincipalId}} identifies its system-assigned identity.
column2:
Use Azure resource identity metadata to identify the principal for role assignments.
Review source

column1: The {{c1::Cognitive Services OpenAI User}} role permits Azure OpenAI inference without model-deployment management.
column2:
Assign the role to the managed identity at an appropriate resource scope.
Review source

column1: Use {{c1::CREATE DATABASE SCOPED CREDENTIAL}} to create authentication configuration for a SQL REST call.
column2:
For this procedure, the credential name must satisfy URL-matching rules.
Review source

column1: For an Azure SQL REST credential, IDENTITY = '{{c1::Managed Identity}}' selects managed-identity authentication.
column2:
The target AI service must authorize that identity.
Review source

column1: A Managed Identity REST credential's SECRET JSON uses {{c1::resourceid}} to specify the token audience.
column2:
The documented property name is lowercase, and its value is not an API key.
Review source

column1: The SQL REST example requests Azure OpenAI tokens for resourceid {{c1::https://cognitiveservices.azure.com}}.
column2:
This audience differs from the specific resource's deployment URL.
Review source

column1: A credential name for sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint must be a valid {{c1::URL}}.
column2:
Its scheme, host, and path scope must match the request according to the documented rules.
Review source

column1: A credential URL for sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint must not contain {{c1::a query string}}.
column2:
Query parameters belong in the request URL, not in the credential name.
Review source

column1: Use {{c1::sys.sp_invoke_external_rest_endpoint}} to invoke an HTTPS endpoint from supported SQL platforms.
column2:
The procedure also supports Azure SQL Database and SQL database in Fabric.
Review source

column1: In SQL Server 2025, enable REST invocation through the '{{c1::external rest endpoint enabled}}' server configuration option.
column2:
The procedure is disabled by default on SQL Server 2025, unlike Azure SQL Database.
Review source

column1: The SQL REST procedure's {{c1::@credential}} parameter names the database-scoped credential to use.
column2:
A matching credential does not replace authorization on the target service.
Review source

column1: The SQL REST Azure OpenAI embeddings example uses @method = '{{c1::POST}}'.
column2:
The input text is sent in the request payload.
Review source

column1: Construct an input payload with {{c1::JSON_OBJECT}}('input': @InputText).
column2:
Use a colon between the JSON key and value.
Review source

column1: Before EXECUTE, store a JSON_OBJECT result in {{c1::a local variable}} and pass that variable to @payload.
column2:
An inline function call is not a valid stored-procedure argument expression here.
Review source

column1: Capture the SQL REST response with @response = @response {{c1::OUTPUT}}.
column2:
Declare the response variable as nvarchar(max) before the call.
Review source

column1: For the SQL REST embedding response, use {{c1::JSON_QUERY}}(@response, '$.result.data[0].embedding') to extract the array.
column2:
JSON_VALUE is for scalar values rather than an entire embedding array.
Review source

column1: The first embedding array in SQL's wrapped Azure OpenAI response is at {{c1::$.result.data[0].embedding}}.
column2:
The endpoint's JSON body is nested under result.
Review source

column1: In the SQL REST JSON response, {{c1::$.response.status.http.code}} holds the actual HTTP status code.
column2:
Log the received status rather than assuming every response is 200.
Review source

column1: The SQL REST procedure returns 0 when the received HTTP status is in the {{c1::2xx}} range.
column2:
The procedure's return code is separate from the HTTP status code in the response.
Review source

column1: If HTTPS completes with a non-2xx status, the SQL REST procedure returns {{c1::that HTTP status code}}.
column2:
An HTTP error response differs from a transport failure that raises an exception.
Review source

column1: GRANT {{c1::EXECUTE}} ON dbo.GetEmbedding TO AIFeatureUsers;
column2:
Underlying REST and credential permissions must also exist in the effective execution context.
Review source

column1: ALTER ROLE AIFeatureUsers {{c1::ADD MEMBER}} [app-service-identity];
column2:
The named principal must already exist as a database user.

column1: Direct SQL REST invocation requires the database permission {{c1::EXECUTE ANY EXTERNAL ENDPOINT}}.
column2:
Restrict this permission rather than allowing applications to bypass a controlled wrapper.
Review source

column1: Using a credential with SQL REST invocation requires {{c1::REFERENCES}} permission on that database-scoped credential.
column2:
This permission is separate from permission to invoke the REST procedure.
Review source

column1: An Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoint uses auth_mode: {{c1::aad_token}} for Microsoft Entra authentication.
column2:
Kubernetes online endpoints do not support this authentication mode.
Review source

column1: For Azure Machine Learning online scoring, request a data-plane token for {{c1::https://ml.azure.com/}}.
column2:
A token for Azure resource management has a different audience.
Review source

column1: Use {{c1::SYSUTCDATETIME()}} to record a UTC datetime2 timestamp for an AI call.
column2:
Use a consistent time basis for monitoring across environments.
Review source

column1: {{c1::ORIGINAL_LOGIN()}} identifies the login that first established the SQL session.
column2:
A shared application login does not distinguish individual human users.
Review source

column1: DATEDIFF({{c1::millisecond}}, @StartTime, SYSUTCDATETIME()) measures AI-call duration in milliseconds.
column2:
Set @StartTime before the request using the same UTC time basis.

column1: After GROUP BY CallerPrincipal, use {{c1::HAVING}} COUNT(*) > 100 to select groups above 100 AI calls.
column2:
Filter the time window with WHERE before grouping.

Workspace roles alone do not configure authentication to an external Azure OpenAI resource.
